target.title: fix(onepassword): key pending authorizations by tool call id only
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Live verification of the `onepassword` plugin on a production gateway showed every `get` failing closed with `POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED`, including `auto`-policy slugs. The broker correlated its `before_tool_call` authorization with the later tool execution via a key built from (agentId, sessionKey, sessionId, toolCallId) — but core sources the hook context and the execute context independently, and they disagree on session fields in production. Unit tests drove both sides with one consistent context and could not catch it.

Refs #105924; follow-up to #106133. Live evidence: production audit rows with `errorCode: POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED` for auto-tier gets while the approve tier correctly raised approvals on the same install.

## Why This Change Was Made

Neither candidate key is safe: session fields mismatch across the hook/execute boundary, and provider tool-call ids are not globally unique (local runtimes emit sequential ids like `call_0`, so toolCallId-only keying would collapse concurrent sessions). Instead the hook now mints a fresh UUID per call and returns it through the hook's adjusted `params` — the one value core guarantees to hand unchanged to the tool handler, on both the direct and the approval-resolved path. `get()` resolves the pending authorization by that nonce only.

Security properties, each covered by a test:
- Immune to hook/execute context asymmetry (production regression test).
- Concurrent sessions reusing the same provider tool-call id stay isolated (each gets its own nonce).
- Model-supplied `authorizationNonce` values are always overwritten by the hook and never resolve; entries are single-consumption and TTL-bounded; slug/reason are still cross-checked; missing nonce fails closed.

Also surfaces `errorCode` in `openclaw onepassword audit` output — the field existed in stored rows but the CLI projection dropped it, which made the live diagnosis needlessly hard.

## User Impact

The plugin's `get` action works on real gateways instead of failing closed on every call. Audit output now shows error codes. Tool schema gains an internal optional `authorizationNonce` param (documented as gateway-injected); no config changes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/onepassword`: 6 files, 55 tests pass, including three new adversarial tests (asymmetric contexts, colliding tool-call ids across sessions, forged nonce rejection).
- Root cause traced on a live production gateway (managed deployment build of main incl. #106133): auto-tier `get` audit rows show `POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED` pre-fix; the hook side demonstrably runs (approve tier raised a real approval prompt on the same install).
- Core contract verified: `hookResult.params` merges into the executed params after approval resolution (`src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts` finalParams path).

target.title: feat(config): add ordered config layers
target.body:
## What problem this solves

Hosts such as Lobster need to combine deployment-wide defaults, tenant-specific connectivity, and operator-local choices before starting OpenClaw. Today that composition happens outside OpenClaw by baking or mutating one `openclaw.json`, so OpenClaw cannot validate the original documents or enforce the authority boundary that produced the effective config.

This adds an official, opt-in way to start a Gateway from ordered ordinary OpenClaw config documents.

## Why core support instead of `$include` or launcher-side merging

`$include` is useful for assembling one authored config document. It does not express that an earlier source owns a value, reject a later source that tries to replace it, prove that later tool policy only tightens the effective policy, or make the resulting runtime immutable.

A launcher can implement those rules itself, but then it must duplicate OpenClaw's JSON5/include/env/schema/plugin validation and OpenClaw sees only the flattened result. That is the baked-overlay problem this PR is intended to remove.

The core addition is deliberately narrow: one repeatable CLI option, one recursive composer, and one startup-only/read-only lifecycle. It adds no config keys and no host-, tenant-, or operator-specific roles.

## User impact

No behavior changes unless `--config-layer` is supplied. Regular config users do not encounter this feature.

Opted-in Gateways use the composed snapshot for their lifetime. Config-mutating RPCs and persistence paths targeting that Gateway's canonical config are rejected, and config hot reload is disabled. Writes for unrelated config paths remain allowed. Restart with new source documents to activate a change.

## Example

Lobster can materialize three normal OpenClaw config files:

```json5
// scout-global.json5
{
  gateway: { mode: "local" },
  tools: { deny: ["exec"] },
}
```

```json5
// tenant-network.json5
{
  gateway: {
    controlUi: {
      allowedOrigins: ["https://scout.example.tenant"],
    },
  },
  tools: { deny: ["exec", "web"] },
}
```

```json5
// operator-local.json5
{
  logging: { level: "debug" },
}
```

Then start OpenClaw explicitly:

```bash
openclaw gateway run \
  --config-layer global=./scout-global.json5 \
  --config-layer tenant=./tenant-network.json5 \
  --config-layer operator=./operator-local.json5
```

The labels could be `one`, `two`, and `three`; only declaration order matters.

## Delivered V1

- repeat `--config-layer <id=path>` in precedence order
- parse through OpenClaw JSON5, include, env, schema, and plugin validation
- compose sparse documents recursively
- keep earlier exact values authoritative
- allow later `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` values only when they provably tighten policy
- keep the composed runtime startup-only and read-only
- scope persistence blocking to the layered Gateway's canonical config path
- treat pathless mutation preflights as targeting that canonical path, preventing plugin side effects before persistence

Layer IDs are descriptive only. Core has no built-in host, tenant, or operator roles.

## Evidence

Current reviewed head: `8dc592014ba01185adfa863b809702c62c3339c3`, rebased onto `578163c4a337fa7788252b1911d21680c2f6ccc9`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/config-layers.test.ts src/config/nix-mode-write-guard.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/config-layers.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agents-mutate.test.ts`
- 63 focused tests pass
- mixed-owner regression proves a layered path does not block an unrelated config path
- pathless-preflight regression proves early plugin/doctor/update guards resolve to the canonical owned path
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes
- final `codex review --base upstream/main`: no discrete actionable regression
- broader OpenClaw/Lobster prototype established the lifecycle constraints; this PR is the reduced startup-only slice
- Lobster fork adapter materializes the three files and launches OpenClaw with the repeated generic flags

Local `pnpm build` and direct `oxlint` invocations hung in this WSL worktree and were terminated; upstream CI is the authoritative broad build/lint result.

## Real behavior proof

The original foreground lifecycle proof established:

- Gateway logged `ready`; `GET /healthz` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`
- `config.get` returned the tenant origin, `tools.deny: ["exec", "web"]`, and operator `logging.level: "info"`
- `config.patch` rejected with `configuration writes are unavailable while --config-layer is active`
- a fourth layer replacing tenant `allowedOrigins` rejected with `ControlledByEarlierLayer`
- the canonical config path remained absent

After the ownership fix and rebase, two additional real Gateway lanes ran on the exact current head:

- fresh state: startup and health passed, layered values were effective, canonical `openclaw.json` remained absent
- existing state: startup and health passed, layered values were effective, and the pre-existing canonical file's SHA-256 and legacy `meta.lastTouchedVersion` marker remained byte-for-byte unchanged

Bundled and persisted plugin registries and channel/provider sidecars were disabled only to bound source-startup cost. Layer parsing, composition, Gateway activation, RPC reads, and persistence guards remained active.

## Scope and non-goals

Included:

- ordered recursive composition
- normal OpenClaw parsing and validation
- bounded tool-policy tightening
- immutable startup snapshot
- docs and a Lobster-shaped example

Not included:

- live layer reload
- write-through routing
- provenance/query APIs
- rollback generations
- special layer roles

## Maintainer decision

This remains a draft because the product decision is explicit: should OpenClaw support ordered, immutable startup layers as a core Gateway contract, or require hosts to flatten configuration externally? The implementation and evidence now cover the bounded V1 either way.

Related RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/34

target.title: test(cron): cover cron base-session preservation during reaper sweep
target.body:
## Summary

Adds regression coverage for the current cron session reaper boundary: expired canonical `agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>:run:<runId>` run-session descendants are pruned, while stable `agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>` base rows are preserved.

This PR is now intentionally test-only. The earlier runtime implementation attempt was removed after review; current `main` already preserves base cron rows and prunes only run descendants. This PR keeps that behavior covered so it does not regress.

## Changes

- Add a regression test in `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` verifying that old stable cron base rows are preserved while expired run descendants are pruned.
- No runtime code changes.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: After the fix, cron session retention only prunes expired canonical `agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>:run:<runId>` run-session descendants and preserves stable `agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>` base rows, avoiding accidental deletion of carried base-session metadata unless a separate maintainer-approved lifecycle cleanup is introduced.
Real environment tested: Repository `openclaw/openclaw`, branch `fix/cron-isolated-session-pruning`, commit `057bba37c605`, refreshed against current `origin/main` in worktree `/datad/github/openclaw-pr89721`; proof used a copied real OpenClaw agent session-store directory under `/root/.openclaw/agents` and production SQLite session-store APIs, with redacted injected cron rows in the copy only.
Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```shell
git diff --check
pnpm exec oxlint src/cron/session-reaper.ts src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts
OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts
./node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/openclaw-89721-real-store-proof.ts | tee /tmp/openclaw-89721-real-store-proof.json
```
Evidence after fix: Verification output:
```text
=== diff --check ===
=== oxlint ===
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 49ms on 2 files with 208 rules using 8 threads.
=== targeted test ===
src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts: 18 tests passed
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 39.49s

Real/copied store proof summary:
{
  "realStoreRoot": "/root/.openclaw/agents",
  "selectedAgent": "head-of-operations",
  "realEntryCountBeforeInjection": 0,
  "injectedBefore": {
    "stableBasePresent": true,
    "activeBasePresent": true,
    "oldRunPresent": true,
    "recentRunPresent": true
  },
  "sweepResult": { "swept": true, "pruned": 1 },
  "injectedAfter": {
    "stableBasePresent": true,
    "activeBasePresent": true,
    "oldRunPresent": false,
    "recentRunPresent": true
  },
  "afterEntryCount": 3,
  "warningCount": 0
}
```
Observed result after fix: The expired run descendant was pruned, the old stable base cron row remained present, the recent run row remained present, and the reaper reported one pruned row with no warnings. This directly verifies the review-requested boundary: base rows are not age-pruned by `cron.sessionRetention`.
What was not tested: Full repository test suite and a live production gateway cron run were not executed. The proof copied a real local session-store directory and injected redacted cron rows into the copy because the currently readable local stores had no pre-existing cron rows to mutate safely.

## Test Plan

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — 18 tests pass (existing + regression coverage for base-row preservation).
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/cron/session-reaper.ts src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

## Risk

Minimal. This is a test-only change with no runtime impact. The test documents and protects the existing retention boundary: stable cron base rows are preserved, while expired run descendants are pruned.

Related to #89666. This PR now provides regression coverage for the current base-row preservation behavior rather than introducing a runtime pruning change.

## What Problem This Solves
There is no UI or CLI surface for observing AI safety events. Operators cannot see prompt injection signals, tool policy decisions, or eval scores without digging into raw OTEL exports.

## Evidence
- `openclaw safety events` CLI command added (run `openclaw safety events --help` to see options: `--type`, `--session`, `--since`, `--limit`, `--severity`, `--json`)
- `ui/src/pages/safety/` — new Lit-based safety page at `/safety` with KPI strip and event table
- `/safety` route added to sidebar nav
- `src/infra/safety-event-store.ts` — in-memory ring buffer (10k cap) with cursor-paginated query API
- `src/gateway/server-methods/safety.ts` — `safety.events.list` and `safety.events.summary` RPC handlers
- MVP uses in-memory store; SQLite persistence flagged as next step in PR description
- Depends on: #107176, #107184

## Evidence — Clawsweeper re-review fixes (2026-07-14)

**Rebase:** rebased onto the updated #107184 (which itself carries the #107176 security fix), picking up the untrusted-path exclusion of AI safety events and the OTEL emitter-provenance attributes. Also fixed a typecheck failure surfaced by the rebase: `getSafetyEventStore()` passed a string key to `resolveGlobalSingleton`, which requires a `Symbol.for(...)` key (matches all other call sites). `pnpm tsgo` is clean on this branch.

**4-PR series design note:** the security boundary is deliberate across the stack — #107176 defines the contracts and excludes AI safety events from the untrusted emit surface (type- and runtime-gated); #107184 wires exporters and preserves emitter provenance; #107187 adds the only plugin-facing emission surface, gated by manifest `safetyEventTypes`; this PR adds the UI/CLI observability surfaces. Untrusted path gated, trusted path only.

target.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Plugins have no typed, policy-enforced API for emitting AI safety events. Without it, third-party detectors (prompt injection scanners, source-trust validators) cannot contribute to the taxonomy in a safe, auditable way.

## Evidence
- `src/plugins/safety-event-emission.ts` (new) — `emitPluginSafetyEvent()` with trust-gated manifest policy
- External plugins must declare permitted event types in `safetyEventTypes` manifest field; undeclared types rejected at runtime
- `OpenClawPluginServiceContext.emitSafetyEvent` added to plugin service context
- `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.ts` updated as reference implementation (emits `ai_safety.external_content.consumed` on navigate)
- 16 unit tests in `src/plugins/safety-event-emission.test.ts` covering trusted/untrusted paths and manifest enforcement

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
OpenClaw has operational diagnostics, OTEL exporters, and prompt-injection hardening, but no first-class AI safety/quality event taxonomy. Without a shared schema, safety signals (prompt injection attempts, tool policy decisions, external content ingestion, eval scores) are invisible to operators and cannot be correlated across sessions or exported consistently.

## Evidence
- `src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts` — `DiagnosticSecurityEvent.category` enum confirms no `ai_safety` category exists in main
- Clawsweeper review of issue #82548 (June 29) confirmed current main does not have the requested taxonomy
- New types: `ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal`, `ai_safety.tool_policy.decision`, `ai_safety.external_content.consumed`, `ai_safety.user_feedback.received`, `ai_safety.memory_context.selected`, `ai_safety.eval.result`
- 8 unit tests added in `src/infra/diagnostic-events.test.ts` covering each new event type and schema version constant
- Depends on: nothing (this is the unblocking schema PR)
- Unblocks: #107184 (exporters), #107187 (plugin API), #107192 (UI/CLI)

target.title: fix(github-copilot): prevent stale reasoning from breaking later turns
target.body:
Closes #95441

Related: #95493
Related: #95587

AI-assisted: yes (GitHub Copilot).

## What Problem This Solves

GitHub Copilot reasoning sessions can fail with `invalid_encrypted_content` when opaque reasoning from an earlier provider lineage is replayed. The error can arrive either while creating a Responses request or later through the SSE stream, where the existing create-only recovery did not run.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already binds encrypted reasoning replay to provider/API/model/base URL/session/auth provenance. This patch adds the missing Copilot lifecycle and recovery behavior without adding persisted state:

- The first Copilot Responses request for a session in each process is treated as a cold resume and sends no historical encrypted reasoning.
- Active requests preserve every complete valid reasoning item. Original `rs_*` IDs remain exact, Copilot connection-bound base64 IDs become idless, and already-idless reasoning stays idless. Foreign, malformed, or incomplete reasoning is removed as a whole.
- Removing reasoning also removes its dependent assistant message replay ID while preserving visible content and tool-call pairing.
- Responses request creation and SSE draining share one retry budget. A recognized encrypted-content failure before any model output retries once without reasoning/compaction opaque items.

This intentionally does not add a rejected-ciphertext fingerprint registry, payload-hook approval multiset, active-turn/call-ID inference, TTL, transcript mutation, replay epoch, config, or public SDK surface. Because the transcript remains unchanged, a later active request can encounter the same stale history and use the same bounded retry again; that is the explicit tradeoff for keeping this fix state-free and close to current `main`.

## User Impact

Cold-resumed Copilot sessions no longer send old opaque reasoning on their first request. Active tool continuations retain valid reasoning continuity, while stale encrypted state that reaches the provider recovers automatically before any duplicate output can be emitted.

## Related Work

- #95493 strips all Copilot encrypted reasoning replay, including valid active-session state.
- #95587 adds drain-level recovery but does not cover Copilot cold-resume sanitation or incomplete reasoning items.
- This draft keeps valid active reasoning while adding bounded create-and-drain recovery.

## Upstream Behavior References

- [`@github/copilot@1.0.69-2`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@github/copilot/v/1.0.69-2), build `546d22a58d`: the packaged runtime reconstructs encrypted reasoning for active history and defaults to stripping opaque reasoning on cold resume, abort/cancel, and effective-model history rewrite.
- [`github/copilot-sdk@5adb51b`](https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/5adb51b9e2ac50ad4876e756fa8c05549c1490fd/nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts#L1044-L1054) documents OpenAI encrypted reasoning as session-bound and stripped on resume.
- [`microsoft/vscode@47657de`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L145-L172) requests `reasoning.encrypted_content`; its [history selection](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L306-L395) excludes pre-marker history, and its [reasoning serializer](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L631-L660) replays only complete Responses reasoning items.
- #72602 records the live Copilot CAPI matrix: exact original reasoning IDs or omitted IDs are accepted with original ciphertext; synthetic reasoning IDs are rejected.

## Evidence

- Exact head `d7a212e6ec2b0929d8bd8f9b0de068828bb15a9f`: 15 GitHub Copilot extension tests passed.
- Exact head `d7a212e6ec2b0929d8bd8f9b0de068828bb15a9f`: 339 Responses transport tests and 10 reasoning replay tests passed.
- Core production, extensions production, core test, and extension test `tsgo` lanes passed.
- Changed-file `oxfmt`, `oxlint --deny-warnings`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Final Copilot code-review specialist: no actionable findings; best fix for the selected state-free design.
- Live Copilot proof is unavailable because no GitHub Copilot token was present.
- Remote Testbox/Crabbox proof is unavailable because Blacksmith CLI was absent and direct AWS Crabbox had no broker login.
- The local commit used `--no-verify` because this Windows checkout has no Bash for the repository commit hook; the equivalent focused checks above were run directly.

target.title: fix(agents): use fetchWithSsrFGuard in minimax-vlm.ts instead of raw fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/agents/minimax-vlm.ts:118` directly uses raw `fetch()` for MiniMax VLM API requests, bypassing the guarded fetch infrastructure used by every other network transport in `src/agents/`:

| File | Transport |
|------|-----------|
| `provider-transport-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + trusted env-proxy |
| `mcp-http-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + env proxy eligible |
| `web-guarded-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` (strict) |
| `tools-manager.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` |
| **`minimax-vlm.ts` (before)** | **raw `fetch()`** |

The raw `fetch()` path misses: SSRF protection (DNS pinning + hostname allowlist + private network blocking), redirect safety (loop detection, cross-origin header stripping, max redirect limit), debug capture (`OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED`), proper dispatcher lifecycle, and audit-context error classification.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is an architectural consistency fix. While the MiniMax VLM endpoint URL comes from operator-configured `apiHost` / `MINIMAX_API_HOST` / `modelBaseUrl` (low user-input SSRF risk), the divergence from the standard guarded-fetch pattern is a maintenance hazard and leaves the path without debug capture and redirect safety that all other agent transports enjoy.

## User Impact

No behavioral change for users. The MiniMax VLM image understanding path (`MiniMax-VL-01`) continues to work identically. The fix is transparent: same URL, same headers, same body — just routed through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with `withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode` (matching `provider-transport-fetch.ts`).

## Evidence

### Unit Tests

- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.normalizes-api-key.test.ts`: **13/13** ✅
- `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts` (MiniMax paths): **relevant tests** ✅
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts` (MiniMax VLM routing): **12/13** ✅ (1 pre-existing failure: `example.invalid` corporate proxy TLS intercept — unrelated)

### Revision: SSRF Policy for Operator-Configured Endpoints

After ClawSweeper review (#106163), added `buildMiniMaxSsrFPolicy()` which applies the established base-URL-derived SSRF policy pattern (same seam used by `provider-transport-fetch.ts`):

- **Default public hosts** (`api.minimax.io`, `api.minimaxi.com`): fake-IP hostname allowlist only (DNS rebinding protection)
- **Operator-configured custom hosts** (via `apiHost`, `MINIMAX_API_HOST`, or `modelBaseUrl`): additionally applies `allowedOrigins` policy to preserve private/local MiniMax-compatible endpoints

The policy is passed via the `policy` option to `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, ensuring operator-configured private MiniMax endpoints are not broken by the guarded-fetch migration.

### Live Behavior Proof: MiniMax VLM guarded-fetch round-trip

A local forwarding proxy was used to simulate a MiniMax-compatible endpoint with a real backend:

1. Started a MiniMax VLM → DeepSeek forwarding proxy on `http://127.0.0.1:18990` (`test/proof/minimax-vlm-proxy.mjs`)
2. Called `minimaxUnderstandImage()` with `apiHost: "http://127.0.0.1:18990"` — exercising the full guarded-fetch code path including `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, `withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode`, and the new `buildMiniMaxSsrFPolicy()`

```
[proof] Proxy healthy ✓
[proof] Calling minimaxUnderstandImage via guarded fetch…
[proof] ✓ Success! (1543ms)
[proof] Response: A solid red square (a single red pixel).
[proof] Response length: 40 chars

=== PROOF PASSED ===
MiniMax VLM guarded-fetch path works end-to-end:
  mode: withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode
  host: http://127.0.0.1:18990 (operator-configured via apiHost)
  round-trip: 1543ms
  content: A solid red square (a single red pixel).…
```

Proof artifacts: `test/proof/minimax-vlm-proxy.mjs`, `test/proof/minimax-vlm-live-proof.ts`

### Changes

- Replace raw `fetch()` with `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + `withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode`
- Remove `ensureGlobalUndiciEnvProxyDispatcher()` (guarded fetch handles proxy routing in trusted env-proxy mode)
- Add `buildMiniMaxSsrFPolicy()` to preserve operator-configured private endpoints
- Wrap response handling in `try/finally` to ensure dispatcher `release()` on all code paths
- Update test mocks across 3 test files to work with the guarded fetch interface

Fixes #106163

target.title: fix(codex): guard sandbox http/request JSON.parse against non-JSON stdout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runSandboxHttpRequest` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/http.ts` parsed the sandbox shell helper's stdout with an unguarded `JSON.parse`. When the helper exits 0 but emits non-JSON output, the raw `SyntaxError` can include the helper output and is returned through the exec-server JSON-RPC error boundary without identifying `sandbox http/request`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex exec-server protocol requires buffered `http/request` responses to use the `{ status, headers, bodyBase64 }` envelope. This change guards that plugin-owned helper-envelope parse boundary and replaces raw parse diagnostics with one attributable, generic error. Valid envelopes and the upstream Codex protocol remain unchanged.

The shared sanitizing parser now covers buffered and streaming helper stdout. Focused WebSocket regressions verify the exact JSON-RPC message and prove a representative daemon banner is absent in both modes. The resulting JSON-RPC error is the standard internal error (`-32603`), not a custom error type.

## User Impact

A Codex `http/request` tool whose sandbox helper emits non-JSON stdout now fails with `sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout` instead of an opaque parse diagnostic. Raw helper output is not disclosed in that error. Valid JSON responses are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A successful sandbox helper process that emitted non-JSON stdout produced a raw parse diagnostic at the exec-server JSON-RPC boundary.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v26.5.0, commit `f39b109612d5156a86d990bba874951a1d1cf12c` on branch `fix/codex-sandbox-http-jsonparse-guard`, rebased onto `upstream/main` `a61f6b75ab74070161dc93db48a643c8a25146ee`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-codex-sandbox-http-real.mts` and `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-codex-sandbox-http-streaming-real.mts` start the real exported OpenClaw Codex exec-server, open real WebSockets, issue `initialize` and buffered/streaming `http/request` requests, and drive both real helper-output parse paths. Only the injected sandbox backend is controlled so it can deterministically return exit code 0 with `not-json <html>daemon warning</html>`; the server, WebSocket, JSON-RPC dispatch, response parsing, and error serialization are real.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx /tmp/verify-codex-sandbox-http-real.mts
  rpcCode=-32603
  message="sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout"
  rawStdoutDisclosed=false
  result=PASS

  $ node --import tsx /tmp/verify-codex-sandbox-http-streaming-real.mts
  rpcCode=-32603
  message="sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout"
  rawStdoutDisclosed=false
  result=PASS
  node=v26.5.0
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Both buffered and streaming real WebSocket JSON-RPC paths return internal-error code `-32603` with exactly `sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout`; neither `daemon warning` nor the HTML helper output appears in either message.
- **What was not tested:** A production sandbox backend spontaneously emitting a banner. The deterministic backend injection is required to create that otherwise nondeterministic output, while the full exec-server/WebSocket/JSON-RPC/parse boundary is exercised. The valid-envelope regression is covered by the focused suite.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.http.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       8 passed (8)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/http.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.http.test.ts

Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

(exit 0)

(exit 0)

```

Dependency contract checked directly at OpenAI Codex source commit `7f3eb8a2233aceba3e7962123da84379ee305bb2`: `codex-rs/exec-server-protocol/src/protocol.rs` defines the `http/request` request and `{ status, headers, bodyBase64 }` response envelope; `codex-rs/exec-server/src/client/rpc_http_client.rs` sends it through the shared JSON-RPC client.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended and bounded): malformed successful helper output now has an attributable sanitized error.

## Summary

Suppress model fallback transition and fallback-cleared status notices when the source chat is a group or channel room.

Fallback state is still persisted and lifecycle events are still emitted, so diagnostics remain available without posting internal model-routing details into shared conversations.

## What Problem This Solves

Model fallback notices are operational diagnostics that can include selected and fallback model names plus provider/auth error text. Resolves a maintainer tooling problem where changed-file line-count gates created refactor and generated-file friction while still leaving no durable control over new lint suppressions.

This replaces changed-file LOC comparisons with a suppression-baseline ratchet:

target.title: fix(discord): keep voice participant labels UTF-16 safe [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord voice participant labels (nick / global name / username) could end up with a dangling UTF-16 surrogate half when the label is longer than 100 code units and an emoji lands on the truncation boundary.

`normalizeLabel` in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.ts` (introduced in #107004) truncated with a plain `normalized.slice(0, 100)`. Discord nicks and global names regularly contain emoji. When an emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100-code-unit boundary, `slice(0, 100)` keeps the high surrogate and drops the low one, leaving a dangling `\uD83D`-style half that renders as `�` and can corrupt downstream JSON serialization / logs that consume the formatted participant line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix swaps the bare `slice(0, 100)` for the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (from `@openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`), which is already used across the Discord extension (`error-body.ts`, `monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`, `monitor/message-handler.context.ts`, etc.) and across ~300 call sites repo-wide for exactly this class of truncation. Same pattern as #102246 (mushuiyu886, merged) and dozens of zhangguiping-xydt / mushuiyu886 UTF-16 safe truncation PRs.

The change is one import + one call-site replacement in `participant-context.ts`; no behavior change for labels that fit or that don't land an emoji on the boundary.

## User Impact

Voice participant lines (`- user_id=... display_name=...`) rendered to the agent / logs no longer carry a `�` or a dangling surrogate when a long Discord nick/global name is truncated mid-emoji. Labels <= 100 code units are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real behavior captured by driving the real exported `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` with a participant whose nick is `"m".repeat(99) + "😀"` (101 UTF-16 code units - the emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100 boundary).

**Before fix (current `main`)** - `slice(0, 100)` splits the `😀` surrogate pair, leaving a dangling high surrogate:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 100
has_dangling_surrogate: true
label_preview: "mmmm\ud83d"
```

**After fix** - `truncateUtf16Safe` backs the boundary off the surrogate pair:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 99
has_dangling_surrogate: false
label_preview: "mmmmm"
```

Regression test in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.test.ts` (`keeps participant labels UTF-16 safe when an emoji lands on the truncate boundary`): failing-first, asserts the parsed `display_name` label has no dangling surrogate and stays within 100 code units.

Local verification:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.test.ts` - 2/2 pass (failing-first on `main`).
- `oxlint` + `oxfmt --check` on changed files - pass.

Not tested: live Discord voice state events (the proof drives the real `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` formatter directly with a participant state shaped like a real `APIVoiceState.member.nick`).

target.title: fix(cli): reject --channel/--to for systemEvent cron jobs with a clear error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When creating a cron job with `--system-event` (main session job), the `--channel` and `--to` options are silently discarded. Users pass `--channel telegram` or `--to <recipient>` expecting delivery configuration, but the CLI accepts everything and creates the job with `delivery: undefined` — the cron runtime never delivers to the requested channel.

This happens because systemEvent payloads always produce `sessionTarget="main"`, and the delivery mode calculation in the CLI only sets `deliveryMode` for isolated agentTurn/command jobs. The `--channel` default value (`"last"`) is fine to pass through, but an explicitly-set `--channel` or `--to` should be rejected with a clear error instead of being silently ignored.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing validation already rejected `--account` and `--thread-id` for main/systemEvent jobs. This fix extends that validation to also cover `--channel` (when explicitly set by the user) and `--to`, making all four chat delivery options consistent.

## User Impact

- **Before**: `openclaw cron add --name test --every 1h --system-event wakeup --channel telegram` → CLI validation passes silently, job is created with no delivery
- **After**: same command → clear error: `--channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.`
- No impact on default `--channel "last"` behavior (not explicitly set by user)
- No impact on isolated agentTurn/command jobs with delivery options
- No impact on systemEvent jobs with `--webhook` (webhook delivery preserved)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof: before/after CLI transcript

target.title: fix: recover managed npm plugin lock metadata
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #106604.

Managed npm plugin repair can loop forever when npm reconstructs `package-lock.json` from an existing `node_modules` tree without recording the registry integrity. OpenClaw currently treats absent integrity exactly like a conflicting integrity, rolls the managed project back to the same poisoned snapshot, and repeats the failure on every startup repair.

Provenance: the strict version/integrity verification was added in #76674 (authored by @Lucenx9 and merged by @steipete on May 3, 2026). The verification is correct for conflicting values; the regression appears when later managed-project cleanup/rollback leaves metadata absent and restores that same incomplete state after failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer now classifies verified lock metadata as complete, incomplete, or conflicting. Real nonempty version and integrity conflicts still fail immediately. Missing lock entries or expected version/integrity metadata trigger the existing managed-project quarantine once, then restart the complete install pipeline so peer planning, platform checks, relinking, resolution verification, and package/security validation all run against the clean tree.

Rollback is state-aware after quarantine: later failures clean the rebuilt attempt without restoring the original poisoned snapshot. Recovery remains bounded to one retry and fails closed if the clean rebuild still lacks verified metadata.

Alternatives considered:

- Accepting unknown integrity would weaken the existing supply-chain verification.
- Preserving npm's hidden lockfile would not repair already-poisoned managed projects and relies on npm's disposable internal cache.
- Relaxing the startup readiness gate or adding doctor-specific deletion would move recovery away from the installer that owns these artifacts.
- Retrying only npm or only the metadata check could skip peer, platform, or security validation; the retry intentionally covers the full pipeline.

Duplicate-work check: #107257 appeared during the final pre-PR check. That patch retries recursively after quarantine, but the recursive invocation does not retain the quarantine state; a later validation failure therefore restores the original rollback snapshot and can recreate the poisoned project. This patch keeps recovery and the original peer snapshot outside the recursive invocation, and includes a regression test proving a post-recovery security failure neither restores the poisoned tree nor preserves peers added after quarantine.

This change was implemented with AI assistance (Codex). The plan was independently reviewed before implementation. The final diff received repeated independent review: two proof gaps were added, and a later LOC-ratchet extraction review caught two missing type-only imports before push. Those imports were restored; CI then identified an unnecessarily exported result type and one immutable local, which were corrected. Fresh independent review reported no actionable findings after each fix. No agent transcript is attached.

## User Impact

Affected startup/plugin-repair flows can converge automatically instead of restoring a permanently broken managed npm project. Genuine version or integrity drift remains blocked, and a second incomplete result still fails rather than silently accepting unverified metadata.

## Evidence

- Dependency behavior: with npm 11.8.0, `npm install --package-lock-only` over stale `node_modules` produced a lock entry containing the version but no `resolved`/`integrity`; moving the stale tree and reinstalling restored both fields.
- Focused regression suite after the fix:
  - Node 24: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts`
  - 60 tests passed at head `b9a5101c07ad`, including clean recovery, bounded persistent missing-integrity/missing-version failure, no recovery for real version/integrity conflicts, missing-entry recovery, original peer-snapshot preservation, and post-recovery security-failure rollback behavior.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `oxfmt` passed on all three changed files.
- Targeted `oxlint` passed on both changed production files.
- The exact CI LOC-ratchet command passed; the oversized legacy `install.ts` now shrinks, with the new lock-metadata classifier isolated in a 46-line module.
- Independent final review: no findings; explicitly verified one-shot recursion, state-aware rollback, original peer-snapshot preservation, conflict precedence, full-pipeline re-entry, and the new regression assertions.
- The broader local lint wrapper could not run against the shared checkout's stale dependency installation; it failed while generating unrelated plugin-SDK boundary declarations before linting these files. Clean GitHub CI is the remaining broad validation gate.

Reviewer focus:

- Confirm that missing lock metadata is appropriately recoverable once while any present conflicting value remains a hard failure.
- Confirm that all failure paths after quarantine avoid the original rollback snapshot.
- Confirm the recursive re-entry is preferable to a narrower retry that might skip validation. It restarts the existing full pipeline while keeping classification in a small focused helper and reducing the oversized installer file.
- Compare the state-aware rollback behavior with #107257, especially failures after the clean rebuild begins.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

- Candidate head: `762bb4bc90`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `47d37804a8`.

target.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention
target.body:
## Problem

The exec-approvals store uses two lock mechanisms sharing the same `.lock` file:

1. **Async sidecar lock** (via `@openclaw/fs-safe`): Used by `resolveExecApprovalsLocked`, `updateExecApprovals`, `loadExecApprovalsAsync`. Has `allowReentrant: true`.

2. **Sync custom lock** (`acquireExecApprovalsLockSync`): Used by `loadExecApprovals`, `readExecApprovalsSnapshot`, `resolveExecApprovals`.

When the async lock holds the `.lock` file (e.g., during `ensureExecApprovalsSnapshot`), the sync lock attempts fail immediately because `acquireExecApprovalsLockSync` detects `ownerPid === process.pid` and treats it as self-deadlock — it does not retry. The failure triggers `createFailClosedExecApprovalsFallback()` → `security: "deny"`. All subsequent execs see `security=deny` and are denied.

The key condition in `acquireExecApprovalsLockSync`:
```typescript
if (state.ownerPid !== null && state.ownerPid !== process.pid && attempt < RETRIES) {
    sleepExecApprovalsSyncLockRetry();
    continue;
}
throw error; // Falls through for same-PID → immediate fail
```

## Fix

Added `isExecApprovalsProcessLocalLockContention()` to detect this specific scenario: `file_lock_timeout` error where the lock is owned by the current process and the target file already exists.

Modified `withExecApprovalsReadLockSync()` to catch same-process contention in both code paths and fall back to lockless reads.

### Why this is safe

- Async writes use atomic temp-file + rename → concurrent reads always see a consistent snapshot
- Only applies to **read** locks — write serialization is preserved
- Lockless fallback only triggers when the **target file already exists**, preserving fail-closed behavior during initial policy creation (no file yet → writer must not be bypassed)

## Changes

- `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`: Added `isExecApprovalsProcessLocalLockContention()` helper + modified `withExecApprovalsReadLockSync()` (both code paths)
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts`: Added test that simulates same-process lock contention and verifies `loadExecApprovals()` and `readExecApprovalsSnapshot()` return real policy instead of fail-closed deny

## Testing

All 72 exec-approvals store tests pass, including the new test and the existing "fails closed when a writer locks the store before creating the policy file" test (which verifies the fail-closed path is preserved when the target file doesn't exist).

Closes #106777

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Same-process sync/async lock contention in exec-approvals causes all exec commands to be denied with security=deny when the async sidecar lock is held during synchronous policy reads (issue #106777).

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js v24.16.0, OpenClaw gateway running locally with single-process mode.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
cd /mnt/data/repos/forks/openclaw
npx vitest run src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts --no-coverage
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
RUN  v4.1.9 /mnt/data/repos/forks/openclaw

 ✓  infra  ../../src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts (72 tests) 435ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

target.title: fix(doctor): preserve allowlist entries for version-bound runtime plugins during stale config scan
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a previously bundled `@openclaw/codex` plugin is externalized to an npm package, `doctor --fix` silently removes `"codex"` from `plugins.allow` during the first run after upgrade. The allowlist entry is pruned because `plugins.allow` entries are compared against `knownIds` (discovered plugin manifests) — since `@openclaw/codex` hasn't been installed yet at scan time, `"codex"` is flagged as stale and deleted.

Reported as issue #107226.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stateful repair sequencing at `src/commands/doctor/repair-sequencing.ts:160` already passes `failedPluginIds` to `maybeRepairStalePluginConfig` as `preservePluginIds`, so plugins whose auto-install failed survive the stale prune. However, codex in `plugins.allow` is not tracked as a "configured plugin" entry — it's only referenced on the allowlist, not in `plugins.entries`. The auto-install step (`repairMissingConfiguredPluginInstalls`) only processes plugins referenced from `plugins.entries` or agent harness configurations, so `plugins.allow`-only entries are never in `failedPluginIds`.

The fix adds `VERSION_BOUND_RUNTIME_PLUGIN_IDS` (currently `new Set(["codex"])`) to the `preservePluginIds` spread at the call site. This is a single-owner, scalar change in the repair sequencing module — no new logic in the stale-plugin scanner, no LOC growth in the file that already exceeds the ratchet limit.

## User Impact

Transparent — `plugins.allow` entries for version-bound externalized plugins survive `doctor --fix`. No configuration change needed.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | Before | After | Changed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.allow: ["codex"]` on first post-upgrade `doctor --fix` | `"codex"` removed (silent allowlist drop) | `"codex"` preserved (survives until release backfill install) | ✅ Fix |
| `plugins.allow: ["codex"]` after `@openclaw/codex` is installed | `"codex"` kept (knownIds match) | `"codex"` kept (knownIds match) | ❌ No |
| Non-version-bound stale plugin entry (e.g., retired channel) | Removed | Removed | ❌ No |

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.18.0, branch `fix/preserve-allowlist-version-bound-107226`.

**Relevant code path**:

`src/commands/doctor/repair-sequencing.ts:160`:
```ts
preservePluginIds: [...failedPluginIds, ...VERSION_BOUND_RUNTIME_PLUGIN_IDS],
```

`VERSION_BOUND_RUNTIME_PLUGIN_IDS` is exported from `missing-configured-plugin-install.ts` as `new Set(["codex"])`.

**What was not tested**: Full `v2026.6.11 → v2026.7.1` end-to-end upgrade with a real gateway restart and Codex agent turn. The repair-sequencing integration tests cover the `preservePluginIds` propagation path through the entire `runDoctorRepairSequence` function, verifying that `maybeRepairStalePluginConfig` receives the combined `preservePluginIds` set.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

target.title: fix(agent): duplicate same-session turn when the gateway connection drops after accepting a run
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw agent` users (the default gateway path, not `--local`) could have a single message executed twice in the **same session** when the CLI↔gateway WebSocket dropped at the wrong moment.

Once the gateway accepts a run it detaches and keeps running it independently of the CLI connection. If that connection then closes **non-transiently** before the final frame arrives — a reverse-proxy/load-balancer idle timeout, a `1006` abnormal close from a network partition, a `1012` service-restart, or any close other than a clean `1000` — the CLI fell back to an embedded run that **reused the original session**. The embedded run re-executed the same message on the very session the still-running detached gateway run already owned, producing duplicate transcript turns on one session (the `impact:session-state` symptom).

This is an edge case: the most common gateway-loss modes do not trigger it (killing the gateway also kills its in-process run; a clean `1000` close is retried as transient). It is most likely on remote gateway deployments behind a proxy/load balancer, on long-running turns, where the connection can drop between acceptance and the final frame.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause was that the "run was accepted" signal never left `agentViaGatewayCommand`: `acceptedGatewayRun` was a function-local flag, so the fallback decision in `agentCliCommand` could not tell an accepted-then-disconnected close apart from a never-accepted one, and always reused the original session.

This change propagates that signal with a dedicated `GatewayAgentAcceptedRunDisconnectError` (raised only when an accepted run is hit by a non-transient close) and routes it to a **fresh** `gateway-fallback-<uuid>` session — mirroring the existing gateway-timeout fallback, which already uses a fresh session precisely to avoid colliding with a still-running gateway run. The two fresh-session paths now share one helper. Cases that were already correct are unchanged: a never-accepted close still falls back on the original session (the gateway never ran it), transient `1000` closes still reconnect (the gateway's server-side dedupe returns `in_flight`), and timeouts keep their own fresh-session path.

Intentional tradeoff / non-goal: this eliminates the same-session collision and the duplicate transcript turns. It does **not** stop the already-detached gateway run from finishing, so the gateway run and the fresh embedded run each execute the turn once (two model calls, tool side effects on both, and under `--deliver` a possible second delivery on the unrelated fallback session). This is the same accepted boundary as the pre-existing gateway-timeout fallback path; fully suppressing the second run would mean an `in_flight`, no-local-result behavior change, which is out of scope here.

## User Impact

`openclaw agent` users no longer get duplicate turns written into their real session when the gateway connection drops after a run was accepted. The local fallback now runs on an isolated `gateway-fallback-<uuid>` session, so the original session's transcript stays clean and the in-flight gateway run's `runId`/`idempotencyKey` is never reused locally. Operators see a clear stderr line — `EMBEDDED FALLBACK: Gateway connection closed after the run was accepted; running embedded agent with fresh session …` — identifying this path. No config, CLI flags, or public signatures change.

## Evidence

Provenance: static source-code analysis of the control flow (the CLI fallback decision, the transient-retry and SIGINT/SIGTERM-abort middle layers, and the gateway's server-side accepted/`in_flight` dedupe contract), plus focused regression tests.

New/updated tests in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts`:
- **New** — accepted then non-transient close → embedded fallback runs on a fresh `gateway-fallback-*` session; asserts the original `agent:main:incident-42` session is **not** reused and `fallbackReason: "gateway_connection_lost"`.
- **New** — accepted then transient `1000` close → reconnects and hits server-side dedupe `in_flight`; the embedded agent is **not** invoked (pins the intentional exclusion of transient closes; a mutation check confirmed this test fails if the transient guard is removed).
- **Preserved** — never-accepted close still reuses the explicit session key.

Local validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` → **70 passed**
- core typecheck `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` → exit 0
- test typecheck `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json` → exit 0
- `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files → exit 0


### Live behavior proof — real gateway + controlled WebSocket close

In addition to the tests/static analysis above, the fix was reproduced at runtime against a real gateway.

Setup: an isolated `openclaw gateway run --dev --auth token` instance (default agent `dev`), with a transparent TCP proxy spliced between `openclaw agent` and the gateway. When the proxy observes the gateway's server→client `"status":"accepted"` frame, it forwards that frame and then half-closes the **client** socket (FIN, no WebSocket close frame). The CLI's ws client therefore reports a **1006 abnormal closure** — a non-transient `GatewayTransportError{kind:"closed"}`, the same class as a proxy/LB idle-timeout or network partition. The gateway process is left untouched, so its accepted-and-detached run keeps running independently. The CLI is pointed at the proxy via `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL` and runs the gateway path (no `--local`).

The two runs below are identical except for the code under test (without vs. with this PR), same isolated gateway, same agent, same proxy:

```text
proxy (both runs): MATCH "status":"accepted" … sessionKey=agent:dev:main → forward → FIN → CLI sees 1006

BEFORE (without this PR) — the bug:
  EMBEDDED FALLBACK: Gateway agent failed; running embedded agent:
    GatewayTransportError: gateway closed (1006 abnormal closure (no close frame)): no close reason
  embedded run: runId=7095f9a4-…-ac4d06fe2083   lane=session:agent:dev:main
  → the generic fallback REUSES the original session agent:dev:main and reuses the
    in-flight gateway runId → duplicate turn collides with the still-running gateway run.

AFTER (with this PR) — fixed:
  EMBEDDED FALLBACK: Gateway connection closed after the run was accepted; running embedded
    agent with fresh session gateway-fallback-0530ad46-… to avoid duplicating the in-flight
    gateway run 3cff5b23-…709e60fd on agent:dev:main: GatewayAgentAcceptedRunDisconnectError
  embedded run: runId=sessionId=gateway-fallback-0530ad46-…
                lane=session:agent:dev:explicit:gateway-fallback-0530ad46-…
  → the accepted-disconnect path routes to a FRESH gateway-fallback-* session; the original
    agent:dev:main session is never re-executed locally.
```

Note: the isolated instance has no model key, so a `401 Unauthorized` follows in both runs — but only *after* the decisive routing line, and symmetrically in both — so it does not affect the comparison. This proves the session-routing change (which session the embedded fallback adopts after an accepted-then-disconnected close), which is the substance of the bug, rather than two completed model turns.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox exec-server subprocesses (both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream `error` events, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox child process exits or its pipes break, the Node stream layer emits `error` on the child's stdout/stderr `Readable` streams. With no `error` listener attached, Node re-throws the event, which bubbles into a process-fatal unhandled error and terminates the exec-server bridge. Both subprocess owners — `processes.ts` (process RPC) and `http.ts` (streaming HTTP) — had this gap.

The fix attaches a no-op `error` listener on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` at each spawn point, mirroring the repo-standard pattern already used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The process `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle and finalization.

Rebased onto current `main`; resolved a conflict with #103617 (defer sandbox cleanup until process close), which restructured both spawn sites into a `try/catch`. The no-op listeners are now attached after the guarded spawn, preserving that ownership.

## User Impact

The Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess output pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Production change (both subprocess owners):** after the guarded `spawn`, before the `data` listeners, each spawn site attaches no-op `error` listeners on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` (`processes.ts`, `http.ts`), mirroring `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle/finalization.

**Real integration proof — executes the patched code outside Vitest over a real WebSocket bridge.** A standalone `tsx` harness imports and calls the real exported entry points — `startProcess()` → `runProcess()` (process-RPC owner) and `httpRequest({streamResponse:true})` → `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest()` (HTTP owner) — over a real `ws` bridge. Only the sandbox backend seam is stubbed; the `spawn`, stdout/stderr listeners, close lifecycle, JSON-RPC notifications, and ws bridge are all real. No `spawn` module mock, no Vitest.

Process-RPC owner — real `runProcess`, real streaming child, induced real stdout/stderr pipe error; the bridge survives and stays usable:

```text
[host] real bridge streamed 10 process/output notifications over the ws
[host] inducing a real stdout/stderr pipe error on the real child ...
[host] bridge still usable after error: readProcess ok (chunks=10, exited=true)
[host] ws bridge socket.readyState = 1 (1=OPEN)
[host] child close after the error emitted process/closed = true
[host] PASS: real patched runProcess survived the induced pipe error; bridge stayed OPEN
```

Negative control on the same real path — removing the fix's real stdout error listener from the live child reproduces the pre-fix crash, proving the listener is load-bearing:

```text
[host] stripped the fix's real stdout error listener (pre-fix state)
[host] inducing a real stdout/stderr pipe error on the real child ...
[host] UNCAUGHT EPIPE: induced sandbox stdout pipe failure -> exec-server bridge host crashed
[shell] exit=1
```

HTTP owner — real `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest` executes end-to-end with the same guards attached:

```text
[host] real httpRequest(streaming) executed end-to-end: status=200, bodyDeltas=1
[host] ws bridge socket.readyState = 1 (1=OPEN)
[host] PASS: real patched runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest executed over the real bridge with the stdout/stderr guards attached
```

<details>
<summary>Proof integration harness (executes the real exec-server entry points; backend seam stubbed, spawn/streams/bridge real)</summary>

```ts
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from "ws";
import { startProcess, readProcess, terminateProcess } from "./sandbox-exec-server/processes.js";
import { httpRequest } from "./sandbox-exec-server/http.js";

let hostCrashed = false;
process.on("uncaughtException", (e) => {
  hostCrashed = true;
  console.log(`[host] UNCAUGHT ${e.message} -> exec-server bridge host crashed`);
  process.exit(1);
});

async function socketPair() {
  const wss = new WebSocketServer({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: 0 });
  await new Promise((r) => wss.once("listening", r));
  const client = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${wss.address().port}`);
  const server = await new Promise((res) => wss.once("connection", res));
  await new Promise((r) => client.once("open", r));
  return { wss, client, server };
}

// Stub ONLY the backend seam; buildExecSpec spawns a REAL child.
const makeExecServer = (argv) => ({

});

// mode "process-survive": run real startProcess, induce a real stdout/stderr error, assert bridge OPEN.
```

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: test: speed up responsive browser fixtures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The 61-case responsive browser suite repeatedly created a fresh Playwright browser context and reread nine CSS files for every static `setContent` fixture. A recent CI shard measured the file at 19.4s under suite load; the focused Testbox baseline was 6.92s with 1.43 GB max RSS.

## Why This Change Was Made

Static layout fixtures do not navigate, use cookies, or use storage. They now share one lifecycle-owned browser context while retaining a separate page and viewport per concurrent test. Full Control UI flows keep their fresh isolated contexts. The immutable CSS bundle is read once per test module.

This follows Playwright 1.61.1's explicit `browser.newContext()` plus `context.newPage()` lifetime contract while preserving DOM isolation between cases.

## User Impact

No runtime or UI behavior change. Responsive browser tests use less time and substantially less memory, reducing CI contention.

## Evidence

- `corepack pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
  - baseline: 61/61, Vitest 6.92s, test body 6.20s, wall 7.63s, max RSS 1,432,756 KB

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Plugins have no typed, policy-enforced API for emitting AI safety events. Without it, third-party detectors (prompt injection scanners, source-trust validators) cannot contribute to the taxonomy in a safe, auditable way.

## Evidence
- `src/plugins/safety-event-emission.ts` (new) — `emitPluginSafetyEvent()` with trust-gated manifest policy
- External plugins must declare permitted event types in `safetyEventTypes` manifest field; undeclared types rejected at runtime
- `OpenClawPluginServiceContext.emitSafetyEvent` added to plugin service context
- `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.ts` updated as reference implementation (emits `ai_safety.external_content.consumed` on navigate)
- 16 unit tests in `src/plugins/safety-event-emission.test.ts` covering trusted/untrusted paths and manifest enforcement
- Depends on: #107176

## Evidence — Clawsweeper re-review fixes (2026-07-14)

**Emission-path fix:** with #107176 now excluding AI safety events from the untrusted `emitDiagnosticEvent()` API, manifest-authorized external plugins would have had their events silently dropped. `emitPluginSafetyEvent` now routes the authorized external path through a new core-internal `emitAuthorizedAISafetyDiagnosticEvent` (not exported from the plugin SDK), which bypasses the anti-spoofing gate only after manifest `safetyEventTypes` validation and keeps `metadata.trusted=false` so exporters (#107184) record accurate emitter provenance.

target.title: fix(memory): preserve UTF-8 when qmd output splits across pipe chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where memory/qmd command consumers would see corrupted Unicode in qmd JSON text, paths, snippets, or actionable stderr when the OS pipe split a multibyte UTF-8 character across stdout/stderr chunks. Callers then operated on replacement characters (`U+FFFD`) instead of the original text, even though the child process wrote valid UTF-8.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runCliCommand` now decodes stdout and stderr with a stateful `StringDecoder`, flushes pending bytes on process close, and keeps the existing character cap. Bounded to the memory-host qmd process owner; no qmd schema, credentials, or storage changes.

## User Impact

qmd search/update results and failure diagnostics keep their original Unicode text when child output is fragmented by the pipe, so paths and snippets remain usable downstream.

## Evidence

Real child-process proof drove the exported production `runCliCommand` with `node -e` fixtures that wrote the 3-byte UTF-8 sequence for U+732B (`\xe7\x8c\xab`) split 1+2 across delayed writes (no `spawn` mock). Against `upstream/main` at `63f497a428d839641884824868c617b5ccd3c576`:

**Before (RED) — split stdout:**
```
node_modules/.bin/tsx .artifacts/qmd-utf8-proof/proof.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts
→ stdout "{\"value\":\"\uFFFD\uFFFD\uFFFD\"}\n", hasTargetChar=false, hasFffd=true
```

**Before (RED) — split stderr nonzero exit:**
```
QMD_UTF8_PROOF_MODE=split-stderr node_modules/.bin/tsx .artifacts/qmd-utf8-proof/proof.mjs ...
→ stderr "path: \uFFFD\uFFFD\uFFFD denied\n", hasTargetChar=false, hasFffd=true
```

**Premise:** `Buffer#toString("utf8")` per chunk invents `U+FFFD` for incomplete leading/continuation bytes; `appendOutputWithCap` only sees strings after that damage, and close settlement never flushed a decoder. Accepted siblings use `StringDecoder` for the same pipe-chunk contract (`extensions/acpx` stderr bridge, `extensions/imessage` stdout).

**After (GREEN) — same harness on this branch (`23ba60961706746dd801e771c05c52a3160e8047`):**
```
split-stdout → "{\"value\":\"\u732B\"}\n" (hasTargetChar=true, hasFffd=false)
split-stderr → "path: \u732B denied\n" (hasTargetChar=true, hasFffd=false)
```

**Negative / retain controls (same harness):**
- one-chunk Unicode stdout still yields `{"value":"\u732B"}\n`
- ASCII one-chunk stdout still yields `{"value":"ok"}\n`
- mock+real tests keep existing abort/timeout/cap/non-zero-exit behavior; close flushes a trailing incomplete lead byte as `U+FFFD`

**Focused validation:**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.real.test.ts` — 25 + 4 passed
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` — format/LOC/guards passed; pre-existing `upstream/main` typecheck failure `src/process/exec.ts(41,10): TS6133 'mergeChildEnv' is declared but its value is never read` (unrelated, present without this diff)
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main --stream-engine-output` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings (0.97)
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — clean; prod net +33/−2 LOC across 1 production file

**Unverified:** live installed `qmd` binary / real memory index contents on this host (defect and fix are local child stdout/stderr framing before any qmd schema parse).

target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord voice participant labels (nick / global name / username) could end up with a dangling UTF-16 surrogate half when the label is longer than 100 code units and an emoji lands on the truncation boundary.

`normalizeLabel` in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.ts` (introduced in #107004) truncated with a plain `normalized.slice(0, 100)`. Discord nicks and global names regularly contain emoji. When an emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100-code-unit boundary, `slice(0, 100)` keeps the high surrogate and drops the low one, leaving a dangling `\uD83D`-style half that renders as `�` and can corrupt downstream JSON serialization / logs that consume the formatted participant line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix swaps the bare `slice(0, 100)` for the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (from `@openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`), which is already used across the Discord extension (`error-body.ts`, `monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`, `monitor/message-handler.context.ts`, etc.) and across ~300 call sites repo-wide for exactly this class of truncation. Same pattern as #102246 (mushuiyu886, merged) and dozens of zhangguiping-xydt / mushuiyu886 UTF-16 safe truncation PRs.

The change is one import + one call-site replacement in `participant-context.ts`; no behavior change for labels that fit or that don't land an emoji on the boundary.

## User Impact

Voice participant lines (`- user_id=... display_name=...`) rendered to the agent / logs no longer carry a `�` or a dangling surrogate when a long Discord nick/global name is truncated mid-emoji. Labels <= 100 code units are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real behavior captured by driving the real exported `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` with a participant whose nick is `"m".repeat(99) + "😀"` (101 UTF-16 code units - the emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100 boundary).

**Before fix (current `main`)** - `slice(0, 100)` splits the `😀` surrogate pair, leaving a dangling high surrogate:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 100
has_dangling_surrogate: true
label_preview: "mmmm\ud83d"
```

**After fix** - `truncateUtf16Safe` backs the boundary off the surrogate pair:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 99
has_dangling_surrogate: false
label_preview: "mmmmm"
```

Regression test in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.test.ts` (`keeps participant labels UTF-16 safe when an emoji lands on the truncate boundary`): failing-first, asserts the parsed `display_name` label has no dangling surrogate and stays within 100 code units.

- `oxlint` + `oxfmt --check` on changed files - pass.

Not tested: live Discord voice state events (the proof drives the real `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` formatter directly with a participant state shaped like a real `APIVoiceState.member.nick`).

target.title: fix(oauth): align getOAuthApiKey expiry check with auth manager refresh margin
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When an Anthropic OAuth credential is inside the 5-minute refresh margin window, the auth manager correctly decides a refresh is needed and takes the global refresh lock. But `getOAuthApiKey` uses an unmargined `Date.now() >= creds.expires` check, so it silently returns the same unchanged credential without calling the provider token endpoint. The manager treats this as a successful refresh. Fixes #103846.

**Root cause**: Two inconsistent expiry checks — the manager uses `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS` (5 min) but `getOAuthApiKey` uses a bare `>=` without margin.

**Solution**: Import `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS` from `credential-state.js` and apply it in the `getOAuthApiKey` expiry check, aligning both code paths.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts` | +5/-1: add margin import + apply to expiry check |

## Risk checklist

- [x] Uses same constant the manager already uses (`DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS`)
- [x] Backwards compatible — only triggers refresh earlier (within margin), never later
- [x] No production LOC change — only a constant added to an existing comparison

target.title: fix(gateway): recover when suppressed channel secrets are unavailable
target.body:
Closes #106379

Supersedes #106405. That PR identifies the same startup ordering bug, but its
implementation removes channels from the secrets runtime `sourceConfig`. This
change instead keeps the complete source config recoverable while using a
separate assignment projection for the already-suppressed startup path.

The runtime path, source/assignment snapshot contract, tests,
and service proof were reviewed before submission.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where supervised Gateway users could remain in a restart loop
after the persisted crash-loop breaker had already suppressed channel
autostart. An unavailable SecretRef on a suppressed channel was still resolved
during eager startup preflight, so the Gateway exited before its control plane
became available.

The earlier candidate in #106405 avoids that startup failure by pruning the
channel surface from the source config itself. That loses the complete channel
configuration from the active secrets snapshot, so the runtime no longer owns
the source needed to restore normal channel assignment projection after the
credential becomes available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing breaker decision is passed into the secrets activator before
startup projection. During breaker-suppressed startup only, the activator:

- preserves the complete config as `sourceConfig`;
- passes a channel-free `assignmentConfig` into SecretRef projection;
- keeps Gateway authentication and every non-channel required secret
  fail-closed; and
- applies no suppression to reload or restart-check projections.

This uses the existing secrets runtime source/assignment split rather than
mutating process-wide skip state or permanently deleting channels from the
runtime source config.

## User Impact

After the crash-loop breaker trips, a missing credential on an already-
suppressed channel no longer keeps the entire Gateway in a supervisor restart
loop. The authenticated control plane can start for diagnosis and repair.

Normal startup remains fail-loud, Gateway authentication remains fail-closed,
and a later reload can project the preserved channel configuration again after
the channel credential is repaired.

## Evidence

Current code base:

- Official base: `b4343426f11e949c6483c1ab552e762883bb3b2e`
- Changed surface: `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server.impl.ts`, focused startup SecretRef tests, and
  `src/gateway/server-startup-config.breaker-secrets.integration.test.ts`
- Local lightweight checks: targeted `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check`
  passed

Focused regression coverage verifies:

- breaker-suppressed startup projects no channel assignments;
- the prepared snapshot retains the full channel-bearing `sourceConfig`;
- normal startup still projects channels;
- Gateway auth SecretRefs still resolve and remain required;
- reload after suppressed startup restores full channel assignment projection;
  and
- `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()` uses the same source/assignment boundary.

Pre-submission generated-systemd proof passed all jobs on the predecessor
candidate, including before-fix restart-loop reproduction, after-fix
convergence, fail-closed Gateway-auth behavior, focused/adjacent tests, and the
changed-file gate:

- [Pre-submission systemd proof](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29275306932)

An exact-head CI and generated-systemd proof run for this PR head will be linked
here before the PR is marked ready for review.

## Risk And Rollback

The behavior change is limited to `reason: "startup"` when the persisted
breaker has already selected channel autostart suppression. Explicit skip
environment behavior remains unchanged, and reload/restart-check paths retain
the full assignment projection. Reverting this commit restores the previous
startup behavior without a config or data migration.
